verdict.rationale: PlayCanvas documents a scriptable Editor API for programmatic scene manipulation and asset management, a REST API on paid plans, and an official Editor MCP server that can modify project data. Its docs also state that the same components are available in the Editor and in code. However, nothing documents full API parity with the UI, and the REST API's scope is undocumented in the evidence. missing for 10: explicit statement or proof of complete UI-to-API parity, documented scope of the REST API, independent hands-on corroboration that UI-only actions (e.g. collaboration, checkpoints, publishing) are API-accessible.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The Editor module provides a comprehensive API for automating and extending the functionality of the PlayCanvas Editor. It allows developers to programmatically interact with the Editor, facilitating tasks such as scene manipulation, asset management, and custom tool integration.
change scenes from code with the Editor API, or from an agent with the MCP server.
It can modify project data and verify the result through the viewport or a running application.
The same components, with the same properties, are available whichever way you build: in the Editor, directly against the engine, in PlayCanvas React and in Web Components.
